resources.string: What the SDK captures once your app is integrated: screen views, taps, text entry, custom events, signals, dialogs, exceptions and session replay of modals. One card per feature, each with the call it makes and where to read the result.

Release-verification checks. Each card verifies one shipped fix against the SDK build this app is running, with the steps to follow and the payload to expect. Intended for regression runs rather than as an integration reference.
Everything here posts to the collector configured in ConnectBasicConfig.properties. Android posts on a foreground timer of about 30 seconds.
Every card sends something to the collector configured in ConnectBasicConfig.properties. Drive a card, then read the posted message there. Android posts on a foreground timer of about 30 seconds.
Long press, double tap, swipe in any direction, pinch and scroll targets on a screen of their own. Compare the gesture type in each posted event with the one the screen reports.
logCustomEvent(name, values) sends a named event with a flat map of values. Read it under customEvent in the posted message.
Sends a signal through logSignal. The nested payload carries an object and an array of objects; the flat one is scalars only. Compare the signal block in the posted type-21 message across platforms.
Uncaught exceptions are reported automatically. For errors your app catches, logExceptionEvent(name, message, stack, unhandled) reports them explicitly. This button throws, catches and reports one.
Opens a platform AlertDialog. logScreenLayoutSetOnShowListener captures its layout when it appears, and logDialogEvent logs the button pressed.
Opens a dialog, which renders in a window of its own, outside the screen it covers. Every element inside it should be selectable in session replay, not just visible in the screenshot.
Text, an input, and buttons — each should appear as its own control in the captured layout.
Foreground, background and orientation changes, logged as custom events tagged with the session id, alongside the SDK\'s own session and logical page.
disable() stops capture. Confirm it on the build in front of you rather than assuming: tap Disable, navigate a few screens, and check that no further layout messages arrive.

Each card names one fix, what to do, and what a fixed build produces. Drive the card, then read the message at the collector configured in ConnectBasicConfig.properties — Android posts on a foreground timer of about 30 seconds.

A card marked \"Baseline only\" has no published artifact carrying its fix. It still runs, deliberately — the failing result is the baseline that makes a later re-run meaningful. Do not read it as a pass.
Log identity — omit both optional args

Type a value starting with SECRET-, then wait for the next post. In the layout message the value should be masked per the config\'s Sensitive rules — capitals to X, lowercase to x, digits to 9, symbols to # — not the text you typed.
In each row\'s accessibility object the label should be masked per the config\'s Sensitive rules — lowercase to x, digits to 9, symbols to #. accessibility.id stays readable on purpose.
The two modal cards below each open a dialog in a window of its own — one opaque over the whole screen, one transparent over the screen beneath — the case that produced an empty control tree.

Nothing to verify in this app: the check is the React Native module compiling against com.ibm.eo / com.tl types, which a native app never does. The card is here so the registry reads the same on every platform.

Scroll until this button sits near the top of the screen, so the WebView below it is fully in view, then capture. The capture skips views that are off screen, so a WebView below the fold is not captured and the check proves nothing.
Opening this screen logged a screen view named:

The referrer is the screen you navigated from. Going back logs the previous screen again, with this one as its referrer — unless a screen view for it is still waiting in the SDK\'s queue, which Android drops as a duplicate until the next post.
Push another detail screen to see the chain advance by one, then pop back through it. Depth %1$d of %2$d.

Every screen view sends a type-2 message carrying the screen name. The platform derives a pageView signal from it; because a mobile screen has no URL, the server-side rule falls back to that name for the signal\'s url.

So each button below is one test of that fallback. Drive them, then check the subscription\'s inferred pageView definition — valid count should rise and the Missing required field: [url] records should stop.

Do not press the Showcase or Verification Log Signal buttons during a run. They send an explicit pageview signal, and inference stands down for a subscription that sends its own — which would read as a pass when it is really a suppression.
Navigate back and re-enter to produce repeat views. A repeat of a name still waiting in the SDK\'s queue is dropped as a duplicate until the next post.

Emits a type-2 screenview whose logical page name is the exact string below. The server-side rule uses that name as the inferred pageView\'s url, so each name is a separate test of the fallback. The empty and null names are only reachable here — navigation cannot carry them.

On Android the SDK treats an empty or null name as no name at all and logs the activity\'s class name instead — MainActivity in this app — so neither arrives as sent. Sent back to back, as Send all does, the second is also dropped as a duplicate of the first while it waits in the queue, so the null line shows ✗.
The type-2 message should carry screenview.name exactly as shown above, and the inferred pageView signal should carry the same string as signalContent.url — valid, not in the invalid-signal topic.
Re-send the same name through the direct call, to compare the navigation-driven message against an explicit one.
